titles.214: Annotatio III §.IV open: Fourth Consociation attempt HEIDELBERGENSE — Otto Henry & Frederick III (1559) pursue Protestant Concord; Heshusius opposes; Melanchthon restores ancient Coena speech
titles.215: Annotatio III §.IV: Melanchthon to the Elector — silence quarrelers; keep one Forma of Paul’s κοινωνία words; declare the Supper’s fruit; the Son is present for man, not for bread
titles.216: Annotatio III §.IV: Some call this fruit-doctrine ‘Cothurnos’ and demand body-in-bread formulas — then invent inclusion, conversion, transubstantiation, ubiquity unknown to learned antiquity
titles.217: Annotatio III §.IV: Heshusius refuses Origen’s σύμβολα and Clement; the same stroke would hit Augustine, Ambrose, Prosper, Dionysius, Tertullian, Bede, Basil, Nazianzen, Theodoret (pp. 379–380)
titles.218: Annotatio III §.IV: Frederick III’s Testament (via Grynaeus) warns sons against turbulent ministers who spawn logomachies against churches agreed on the foundation in Christ
titles.219: Annotatio III §.IV close: Turbulence breeds political and church division and Papal opening — princes must remove the unamendable, yet not strip pastors of moderated correction; stop before §.V Sendomiriense

latin.214:
§. IV.
Francofurtano Molimini, ob annorum Connexionem, adnectere liceat HEIDELBERGENSE, Ottone Henrico & Friderico III. Electoribus Palatinis Autoribus, in Palatinatu, Anno 1559., summo studio Protestantium Concordiam molientibus, & turbulento admodum (Judice Schmidlino apud Hospinianum Concord. Discord. cap. 46. haud procul a fine, Nov. Edit. Genev. p. m. 409) Heshusio sese opponentibus, ex consilio verò Philippi Melanchthonis, modos de Sacra Coena loquendi veterum, reducentibus. Consilium Melanchthonis, Annô ante obitum praeterpropter dimidio, datum, exstat Parte posteriori Consiliorum & Judiciorum ejus Theologicorum, Friderico III. Electori suppeditatum pag. 378. & seqq.
latin.215: Verba quaedam memorari juvat: Probo (scribit Melanchthon ad Electorem) Consilium Illustrissimi Electoris, quod rixantibus utrinque mandavit silentium, ne distractio fiat in tenera Ecclesia & infirmi turbentur in illo loco & vicinia, & optarem rixatores in utraque parte abesse. Secundò, remotis contentiosis, prodest reliquos de una Forma verborum convenire & in hac controversia optimum est retinere verba Pauli: Panis quem frangimus κοινωνία ἐστὶ τοῦ σώματος, & copiosè de fructu caenae dicendum est, ut incitentur Homines ad amorem hujus pignoris & crebrum usum; & vocabulum κοινωνία declarandum est. Paucisque interfertis: Adest, inquit Melanchthon, Filius Dei in Ministerio Evangelii & ibi certè efficax est in credentibus, ac adest, non propter Panem, sed propter Hominem, sicut inquit: Manete in me, & ego in vobis. Item: Ego sum in Patre meo, & vos in me & Ego in vobis. Et his veris Consolationibus facit nos sibi membra & testatur se corpora nostra vivificaturum esse.
latin.216: Sed hanc veram & simplicem Doctrinam de fructu nominant quidam Cothurnos, & postulant dici, an sit Corpus in Pane, aut Speciebus panis, quasi verò Sacramentum propter Panem & istam Papisticam Adorationem institutum sit. Postea fingunt, quomodo includant Pani; Alii Conversionem, alii Transsubstantiationem, alii Ubiquitatem excogitarunt. Haec portentoze omnia ignota sunt eruditae Vetustati.
latin.217: Negat Heshusius, se assentiri Origini, qui nominat Panem & Vinum σύμβολα σώματος καὶ αἵματος; rejicit calumniosè Clementem Alexandrinum; pronunciabit eodem modo de Augustino, Ambrosio, Prospero, Dionysio, Tertulliano, Beda, Basilio, Nazianzeno, qui nominat ἀντίτυπον σῶμα; Theodoreto, qui ait de Pane φύσιν & μεταβαλών pag. 379. & 380.
latin.218: Memoratu quoque digna Pericopa ex Testamento Sereniss. Electoris Friderici III. ad Filios Celsissimos, ex Joh. Jac. Grynaeo excerpta, & pia Commonefactioni ejus de Officio piorum Hominum, qui necesse habent versari ad Catadupa Anathematismorum adversus sanam doctrinam de Eucharistia à pag. 47. ad pag. 49. subjuncta, his verbis: Tertiò ac praecipuè moneo ac hortor charissimos filios meos, ut sibi quam diligentissimè à turbulentis tam Ecclesiarum quam Scholarum ministris caveant, qui nunc in Religionis & fidei negotiis omnis generis contentiones, logomachias & exitiales condemnationes in pias Ecclesias & Scholas, quae tamen in fundamento, & praecipuis Christianae Religionis capitibus consentiunt, & salutem suam unà nobiscum in unicum nostrum Servatorem Jesum Christum collocant, ex vera ambitione & perverso zelo, ac praetextu ministerii sui, per quod Sanctum Spiritum mundum arguere volunt, idque indictâ causa, nec sine scandalo introducere, & non minùs, quàm in execrando Papatu factum est, tam in Magistratuum, quam in subditorum conscientias dominari, & sibi novum quendam primatum passim erigere ac constituere conantur.
latin.219: Ex qua re sanè non tantùm in Politica, & in Ecclesiastica gubernatione distractiones & exulcerationes animorum, utriusque illius gubernationis perturbatio & interitus sequitur: verùm etiam Papa & ejus satellitio praebetur occasio, veram nostram Christianamque Religionem ferro, flammâ, exiliis, aliisque innumeris suppliciis persequendi, suamque tyrannidem hoc modo stabiliendi: quae res quantas & quàm miserandas pepererit distractiones, miserias & calamitates, etiam nostrâ hac aetate nimis proh dolor multa in Electorum aliorumque Germaniae Principum provinciis, nec non apud exteras & vicinas gentes extant exempla. Ex quibus meritò omnes Christiani Principes, Ecclesiae & Scholae, exemplum sibi quod ex usu sit, capere, ideoque summoperè à turbulentis istis hominibus, & pacis ac tranquillitatis publicae inimicis sibi cavere, nec permittere, ut ab illis occupentur, & vel inter sese, vel contra alios exacerbentur, aut à se invicem divellantur, ac distrahantur, sed potiùs ejusmodi homines vitare & fugere, & si nulla in eis emendationis spes appareat, prorsus à se removere debebunt: sicuti hac de re inter me aliosque Electores & Principes non semel ex jam dictis aliisque pluribus piis & gravibus causis convenit. Sic tamen, ut hac ratione nihil piis Ecclesiarum ministris, quod attinet ad debitam eorum, quae quotidie offeruntur, vitiorum reprehensionem & correctionem, & errorum, Christiana adhibitâ moderatione & aequitate, ex verbo Dei desumtam refutationem, quae non ad destructionem, sed ad aedificationem, dirigenda & instituenda est, derogaretur.

pass_a.214: §. IV. To the Frankfurt Effort, on account of the connection of the years, it is permitted to join the HEIDELBERG one, Otto Henry and Frederick III the Electors Palatine being the authors, in the Palatinate, in the year 1559, with highest zeal attempting the Concord of the Protestants, and opposing themselves to the altogether turbulent Heshusius (Schmidlin judging, in Hospinian Concordia Discordans ch. 46 near the end, new Geneva edition p. approximately 409), but from the counsel of Philip Melanchthon restoring the ancient modes of speaking about the Sacred Supper. Melanchthon’s counsel, given about half a year before his death, stands in the later Part of his Theological Counsels and Judgments, supplied to Elector Frederick III, p. 378 and following.
pass_a.215: It helps to remember certain words: I approve (Melanchthon writes to the Elector) the Counsel of the Most Illustrious Elector, that he commanded silence to those quarreling on both sides, lest distraction arise in the tender Church and the weak be troubled in that place and neighborhood, and I would wish the quarrelers on either side to be away. Secondly, the contentious having been removed, it is profitable that the rest agree on one Form of words, and in this controversy it is best to retain the words of Paul: The bread which we break is the κοινωνία of the body, and one must speak copiously of the fruit of the Supper, that men may be stirred to love of this pledge and frequent use; and the word κοινωνία must be declared. And with a few things inserted: The Son of God is present, says Melanchthon, in the Ministry of the Gospel and there he is certainly efficacious in believers, and he is present not on account of the Bread but on account of Man, as he says: Abide in me, and I in you. Likewise: I am in my Father, and you in me and I in you. And by these true Consolations he makes us members to himself and testifies that he will vivify our bodies.
pass_a.216: But this true and simple Doctrine concerning the fruit certain ones name Cothurni (tragic boots / inflated speech), and they demand that it be said whether the Body is in the Bread, or in the Species of bread, as if truly the Sacrament were instituted on account of the Bread and that Papistic Adoration. Afterwards they invent how they may enclose it in the Bread; some have devised Conversion, others Transubstantiation, others Ubiquity. All these portentous things are unknown to learned Antiquity.
pass_a.217: Heshusius denies that he assents to Origen, who names the Bread and Wine σύμβολα of the body and blood; he rejects calumniously Clement of Alexandria; he will pronounce in the same way concerning Augustine, Ambrose, Prosper, Dionysius, Tertullian, Bede, Basil, Nazianzen, who names an ἀντίτυπον body; concerning Theodoret, who says of the Bread φύσιν and μεταβαλών — pages 379 and 380.
pass_a.218: Also worthy of memory is a Pericope from the Testament of the Most Serene Elector Frederick III to his Most High Sons, excerpted from Johann Jacob Grynaeus, and joined to his pious Admonition concerning the Office of pious Men who must dwell by the Cataracts of Anathemas against the sound doctrine of the Eucharist, from p. 47 to p. 49, in these words: Thirdly and chiefly I warn and exhort my dearest sons to guard themselves most diligently from turbulent ministers of both Churches and Schools, who now in affairs of Religion and faith introduce contentions of every kind, logomachies and deadly condemnations against pious Churches and Schools which nevertheless agree in the foundation and the chief heads of the Christian Religion, and place their salvation together with us in our only Savior Jesus Christ, from true ambition and perverse zeal, and under pretext of their ministry, through which they wish the Holy Spirit to convict the world, and that with the cause undeclared, and not without scandal, and no less than was done in the execrable Papacy they try to dominate the consciences of Magistrates as of subjects, and to erect and establish for themselves a certain new primacy everywhere.
pass_a.219: From which matter certainly there follows not only in Political and in Ecclesiastical government distractions and ulcerations of minds, disturbance and ruin of either government: but also opportunity is afforded to the Pope and his retinue of persecuting our true and Christian Religion with iron, flame, exiles, and other innumerable punishments, and of establishing their tyranny in this way: which matter how great and how miserable distractions, miseries and calamities it has brought forth, even in this our age — alas too many — examples stand in the provinces of Electors and other Princes of Germany, and also among foreign and neighboring peoples. From which deservedly all Christian Princes, Churches and Schools ought to take for themselves an example that is of use, and therefore especially to guard themselves from those turbulent men and enemies of public peace and tranquillity, and not permit that they be occupied by them, and either among themselves or against others be exasperated, or be torn and distracted from one another, but rather to avoid and flee such men, and if no hope of amendment appears in them, to remove them entirely from themselves: just as on this matter it has more than once been agreed between me and other Electors and Princes from the already stated and many other pious and weighty causes. Yet so, that by this reason nothing should be derogated from pious ministers of the Churches as concerns the due reproof and correction of vices that are offered daily, and the refutation of errors drawn from the word of God with Christian moderation and equity applied, which is to be directed and instituted not to destruction but to edification.

214: §. IV. To the Frankfurt attempt, by the link of years, one may join the Heidelberg one.

Its authors were Electors Palatine Otto Henry and Frederick III, in the Palatinate in 1559 — pressing hard for Protestant Concord, and opposing the very turbulent Heshusius (so Schmidlin in Hospinian, Concordia Discordans ch. 46 near the end, new Geneva ed. p. ~409).

From Philip Melanchthon’s counsel they restore the Fathers’ ways of speaking about the Sacred Supper. That counsel, given about half a year before Melanchthon’s death, stands in the later part of his Theological Counsels and Judgments supplied to Elector Frederick III (p. 378ff).
215: Some of Melanchthon’s words to the Elector are worth keeping: he approves the Elector’s counsel that both sides’ quarrelers be silenced, lest the tender church split and the weak nearby be troubled — and he wishes such quarrelers gone from either party.

Second, once the contentious are removed, the rest should agree on one Forma of words; best here is to keep Paul’s: the bread we break is the κοινωνία of the body — and to speak richly of the Supper’s fruit so people love this pledge and use it often, declaring what κοινωνία means.

Melanchthon inserts: the Son of God is present in the ministry of the Gospel and efficacious in believers — present not for the bread but for the man ("Abide in me…"; "I am in my Father, and you in me…"). By these consolations he makes us his members and promises to vivify our bodies.
216: Yet some brand this true, simple fruit-doctrine as Cothurnos (inflated tragic boots) and demand a yes/no: is the body in the bread, or in the species of bread — as if the sacrament were instituted for the bread and that papistic adoration.
Then they invent how to shut it into the bread; some invent Conversion, others Transubstantiation, others Ubiquity.
All these portentous inventions are unknown to learned antiquity.
217: Heshusius refuses assent to Origen, who calls bread and wine σύμβολα of body and blood; he calumniously rejects Clement of Alexandria.

The same verdict would fall on Augustine, Ambrose, Prosper, Dionysius, Tertullian, Bede, Basil, and Nazianzen (who speaks of an ἀντίτυπον body), and on Theodoret, who says of the bread φύσιν and μεταβαλών (pp. 379–380).
218: Also worth remembering is a passage from Elector Frederick III’s Testament to his sons, taken from Johann Jacob Grynaeus and joined to his pious admonition on the duty of godly men who must live beside the cataract of anathemas against sound eucharistic teaching (pp. 47–49).

Third and above all, he warns his dearest sons to watch most carefully against turbulent ministers of churches and schools who, in religion and faith, spawn every kind of contention, word-fight, and deadly condemnation against pious churches and schools that still agree on the foundation and the chief heads of Christian religion and place their salvation with us in Christ alone.

From ambition and crooked zeal, under pretext of a ministry by which they claim the Spirit should convict the world, they introduce this without declared cause and not without scandal — trying, no less than in the cursed Papacy, to dominate magistrates’ and subjects’ consciences and raise a new primacy for themselves everywhere.
219: From such turbulence follow not only political and church distraction and ulcerated minds — disturbance and ruin of both governments — but also an opening for the Pope and his retinue to persecute our true Christian religion with iron, flame, exile, and countless other punishments, and so to fix their tyranny.
How great and miserable the resulting divisions and calamities are, even our own age shows too many examples in Electors’ and other German princes’ lands, and among neighboring peoples.

Christian princes, churches, and schools should therefore take the lesson: guard hard against these turbulent enemies of public peace; do not let them seize posts, inflame parties, or tear people apart; avoid and flee them; and if no hope of amendment appears, remove them outright — as Frederick says he and other Electors and princes have more than once agreed for these and other pious, weighty reasons.

Yet nothing in that counsel should strip godly church ministers of due daily reproof and correction of vices, or of error-refutation drawn from God’s word with Christian moderation and equity — aimed at building up, not tearing down.
